note: Both sets capture the core controller goals, operating ranges, filter type and variable definitions correctly with supporting quotes. Set A additionally covers the sole-feedback-input fact for both controllers and the important statement that nacelle-yaw control actions were not developed, which Set B omits. Set B instead adds a near-trivial claim that the baseline control system was based on the conventional design approach and repeats the nonpower-production claim under two entity names. Set A's extra coverage of an important fact outweighs its redundancy, though it repeats the feedback-input and filter-type facts several times.
remarks: Set A states the generator-torque feedback input three times and the blade-pitch feedback input twice (differing only in the conditions field), and the filter type twice; these are the same facts restated. Set B omits the nacelle-yaw-angle statement, a notable design fact on the page. Neither set extracts the filter equations (7-1, 7-2, 7-3a) or the definitions of alpha, n, Ts and fc, which are the main quantitative content of Section 7.1.
